req.title: Login required for delete
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they POST /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-014 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who POST to /<id>/delete are redirected to /auth/login. The test suite covers: (1) positive case — anonymous POST to a valid post id triggers a 302 redirect to /auth/login; (2) negative case — an authenticated user POSTing to delete their own post succeeds (not redirected to login), confirming the guard only fires for anonymous users; (3) boundary case — anonymous POST to post id=1 (lowest valid id in dataset) still redirects; (4) state-transition case — user logs out then attempts delete, confirming session state drives the redirect; (5) decision-table case — anonymous POST to a non-existent post id still redirects to login before any 404 logic fires. All assertions use exact status codes and exact Location header values to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_anonymous_delete_redirects_to_login
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database pre-loaded with seed data (post id=2 exists, author_id=1)
trace: R-FLASKR-014: anonymous POST /<id>/delete must redirect to /auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_anonymous_delete_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_anonymous_delete_redirects_to_login()

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_authenticated_delete_does_not_redirect_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    assert login_r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    assert r.headers['Location'] != '/auth/login'

test_authenticated_delete_does_not_redirect_to_login()

Client logs in as Rahul then logs out (session cleared)

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_logout_then_delete_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    logout_r = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert logout_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_logout_then_delete_redirects_to_login()
